children: Oil and gas producers in the U.S. Gulf said Sunday they are restarting production that was shut-in last week by Hurricane Isaias, which came ashore at the Florida panhandle last Friday night.

said it is returning workers to its Gulf platforms and restoring full production after it had temporarily curbed production at five facilities; the company had said its Pascagoula, Mississippi, plant remained operational and has reported no storm-related damage.
U.S. oil companies had shut in ~1.3M bbl/day, or 63% of total U.S. production in the Gulf, ahead of the hurricane.
Refineries on the Gulf Coast had been running at 95% of total capacity, so there was no slack in the system to make up for lost production, but this concern appears to have been unrealized.
